stem: Complete this statement about Anterior and Lateral Compartments of the Leg: The lateral compartment everts the foot at the subtalar joint, is innervated by the superficial fibular nerve, and contains two muscles: fibularis longus (superficial and larger; from head and upper two-thirds of lateral fibula to medial cuneiform and ____; plantarflexes and everts) and fibularis brevis (shorter and deeper; from inferior two-thirds of lateral fibula to dorsal base of 5th metatarsal; everts and weakly plantarflexes).

explanation.correct: Anterior and Lateral Compartments of the Leg: The lateral compartment everts the foot at the subtalar joint, is innervated by the superficial fibular nerve, and contains two muscles: fibularis longus (superficial and larger; from head and upper two-thirds of lateral fibula to medial cuneiform and base of 1st metatarsal; plantarflexes and everts) and fibularis brevis (shorter and deeper; from inferior two-thirds of lateral fibula to dorsal base of 5th metatarsal; everts and weakly plantarflexes).

subtopic: Gluteal Region: Boundaries, Layers, and Bursae
stem: Complete this statement about Gluteal Region: Boundaries, Layers, and Bursae: Its muscles are arranged in two layers: the superficial layer (gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, and tensor fasciae latae), which mainly extend, abduct, and medially rotate the thigh; and the deep layer of short lateral rotators (piriformis, obturator internus, superior and inferior gemelli, and quadratus femoris), covered by the inferior half of gluteus maximus, which laterally rotate the thigh and ____.

explanation.correct: Gluteal Region: Boundaries, Layers, and Bursae: Its muscles are arranged in two layers: the superficial layer (gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, and tensor fasciae latae), which mainly extend, abduct, and medially rotate the thigh; and the deep layer of short lateral rotators (piriformis, obturator internus, superior and inferior gemelli, and quadratus femoris), covered by the inferior half of gluteus maximus, which laterally rotate the thigh and stabilize the hip joint.

explanation.correct: Plantar Layers 3 and 4 of the Foot: Layer 4 contains the interossei, all innervated by the lateral plantar nerve (S2, S3): 3 plantar interossei (from medial sides of metatarsals 3 to 5 to extensor hoods and proximal phalanges of digits 3 to 5; adduct toes 3 to 5) and 4 dorsal interossei (from adjacent sides of metatarsals 1 to 5 to the medial proximal phalanx of toe 2 and lateral proximal phalanges of toes 2 to 4; abduct toes 2 to 4 away from the 2nd toe reference axis).

subtopic: Pulmonary Cavities, Pleura, and Clinical Anatomy
stem: Complete this statement about Pulmonary Cavities, Pleura, and Clinical Anatomy: Clinical disorders include pneumothorax (air in the pleural cavity from spontaneous rupture, lung disease, trauma, or chest tube procedures—appearing black on chest X-ray), pleural effusion (____ expansion—appearing white/gray on chest X-ray), and hemothorax (blood in the pleural cavity from trauma, ruptured vessels, malignancy, or anticoagulation for pulmonary embolism—also appearing white/gray on chest X-ray).

explanation.correct: Pulmonary Cavities, Pleura, and Clinical Anatomy: Clinical disorders include pneumothorax (air in the pleural cavity from spontaneous rupture, lung disease, trauma, or chest tube procedures—appearing black on chest X-ray), pleural effusion (excess fluid preventing lung expansion—appearing white/gray on chest X-ray), and hemothorax (blood in the pleural cavity from trauma, ruptured vessels, malignancy, or anticoagulation for pulmonary embolism—also appearing white/gray on chest X-ray).

topic: Blood Supply, Veins and Lymphatics of the Lower Limb
subtopic: Lymphatic Drainage of the Lower Limb
stem: Complete this statement about Lymphatic Drainage of the Lower Limb: Deep lymph nodes comprise deep inguinal nodes (along the femoral vein draining superficial inguinal and popliteal nodes), popliteal nodes (____ in the popliteal fossa draining the skin of the lateral foot and back of the leg, deep leg and foot structures, and knee lymphatics), and variably present anterior tibial nodes (on the upper anterior tibial artery draining the anterior leg into popliteal nodes).

explanation.correct: Lymphatic Drainage of the Lower Limb: Deep lymph nodes comprise deep inguinal nodes (along the femoral vein draining superficial inguinal and popliteal nodes), popliteal nodes (3 to 6 nodes in the popliteal fossa draining the skin of the lateral foot and back of the leg, deep leg and foot structures, and knee lymphatics), and variably present anterior tibial nodes (on the upper anterior tibial artery draining the anterior leg into popliteal nodes).

stem: Complete this statement about Fascial Spaces of the Hand and Space of Parona: In the distal forearm, the space of Parona extends from the proximal margin of the carpal tunnel to the mid-forearm, roofed by flexor digitorum profundus tendons distally and ____, bounded by flexor carpi ulnaris medially and flexor pollicis longus laterally, with a floor formed by pronator quadratus distally and the interosseous membrane in its proximal two-thirds.

explanation.correct: Fascial Spaces of the Hand and Space of Parona: In the distal forearm, the space of Parona extends from the proximal margin of the carpal tunnel to the mid-forearm, roofed by flexor digitorum profundus tendons distally and flexor digitorum superficialis proximally, bounded by flexor carpi ulnaris medially and flexor pollicis longus laterally, with a floor formed by pronator quadratus distally and the interosseous membrane in its proximal two-thirds.
